correctness.rationale: The exact ratio recursion is algebraically derived from the positive two-patch migration matrix. In log coordinates each of the two Bernoulli maps has global Lipschitz constant at most |(1-theta)/(1+theta)|<1, guaranteeing unique invariant law and compact support attractor. The extremal positive root R of a*tau*R^2+(1-a)*R-tau=0 is calculated; first-level image intervals are [1/R,X] and [1/X,R]. They cover the hull iff X>=1, equivalent to tau<=a/(a^2+a+1), hence the two q thresholds. Otherwise strong separation and contraction give a Cantor set, while tau=1 gives a singleton. The q-duality is proved using the inversion intertwining identity and fair branch symmetry. A standalone checker replayed 2,383 exact-rational and floating-root consistency assertions; finite tests are expressly not relied upon as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Stationary habitat-abundance ratios are a meaningful ecological diagnostic, and the parameter-complete reentrant interval/Cantor/singleton/interval classification identifies when entire bands of imbalance are structurally impossible. The paired q versus qdagger equality reveals genuine one-time stationary-marginal nonidentifiability with survival s and growth contrast fixed. These are motivated qualitative structural facts about the original ecological stochastic model, not a generic urn count, marginal restatement or arbitrary narrow slice. Limits: idealized two-state iid process, no noisy-data inference or persistence assertion.
